To support non-uniform costs, a change is required. Intra wing edges has gained an explicit weight data attribute and inter-wing junctions now has an associated cost stored in a separate dictionary, since junctions connect 2 separate wings, and so don't exclusively belong to either. For these to occur, the Graph ADT will require new operations: get_edge_weight(u, v) -> Integer where u and v are nodes, needed to acquire real traversal cost. The add_edge() ADT needs to be updated to allow for weight attributions: add_edge(u, v, weight) -> None . The Dictionary ADT requires no change but will be instanced a 3rd time to hold junction costs. The Queue ADT is no longer functional for the weighted facility, and so a Priority Queue needs to be implemented instead to allow for Dijkstra exploration by smallest cost rather than old FIFO strcutre (first-in first-out). Operations needed are: insert(priority, path) -> None, pop() -> (priority, path) lowest priority element , is_empty() -> Boolean , size() -> Integer . All other ADT's are unchanged.

Edges weights are stored as a property of the edge itself rather than on demand computing. Once facility is defined, the required edges/corridors are queried, and their weight attribute is read and returned -> get_edge_weight(u, v) -> Integer . Junction costs will be retrieved via this ADT operation.

At construction, the graph ADT's are filled with each wings weight model, where each edge receives the weight cost attribute. These values are then stored. The get_edge_weight() signature remains the same regardless, checking if u and v are in same wing and so querying intra_wing or inter_wing databases as required.

Dijkstra's is a suitable algorithm for finding min-cost paths in the weighted facility. It will calculate the shortest costs & paths between key nodes (entry, supplies, and 2 exits). This subroutine acts as a key preprocessing tool needed for branch-and-bound, the main route selector that has been unchanged and carried over from amendment 1 to this amendment 2. The Dijkstra algorithm acts as a replacement for the initial BFS processor, as edges are now weighted rather than of uniform cost. The algorithm repeatedly pops lowest cost node from priority queue and finalises it, guaranteeing that no future cheaper path to it can be formed. 

While Dijkstra has a known defect, the existence of negative edge weights can stop it returning accurate min-cost paths, this defect is acceptable here as the cost models for all wings are of 1 or greater (wing alpha has uniform cost of 1, and wing beta is 1 + floored(col / 3), with gamma+ being seed randomised but always positive). Due to this, the defect doesn't occur, and Dijkstra greedy finalisation is provably correct. This non-negativity is also the basis for the branch and bound pruning condition, since no further exploration of a branch can provide a lower cost, a branch can be pruned when its current cost or cost to exit becomes higher than best - true optimum branch doesn't get pruned. 

Key structural change - while memo 1 used BFS - explored based on FIFO queue (exploration order = cost order), in a weighted non-uniform network, the equivalence is broken and so priority queue ADT replaces original queue. Nodes are now explored based on lowest cost rather than insertion order.

Key trade-off is that algorithm correctness depends on non-negative-weights in facility. If in future cost model, negative edge weights are introduced, Dijkstra will return greater than optimum results.

   exitB <- GET_EXIT(graph, 'Exit B')
   wings = graph['wings']
   junctions = graph['junctions']
   keyElements <- LIST(supplies) + [exitA, exitB]
   dist <- empty Dictionary
   paths <- empty Dictionary
   FOREACH u IN [entry] + LIST(supplies) DO
      dist[u] <- empty Dictionary
      paths[u] <- empty Dictionary
      SHORTEST_PATHS_DICT_CONSTRUCTOR(graph, u, keyElements, dist, paths, wings, junctions)
   END FOR

   best <- STATE_SPACE_SEARCH(entry, LIST(supplies), 0, [], dist, exitA, exitB, INFINITY, null)
   bestOrder <- best.order
   bestCost <- best.cost

   fullPath <- [entry]
   current <- entry
   FOREACH node IN bestOrder DO
      segment <- paths[current][node]
      FOREACH i <- 1 TO LENGTH(segment) - 1 DO
          APPEND(segment[i], fullPath)
      END FOR
      current <- node
   END FOR

   RETURN {route: fullPath, cost: bestCost}
END FUNCTION

FUNCTION INTRA_WING_NEIGHBOURS(node: Node, wing: Graph) -> Set[Node]
  RETURN wing.NEIGHBOURS(node)
END FUNCTION

FUNCTION INTER_WING_NEIGHBOURS(node: Node, junctions: List[Pair[Node, Node]]) -> Set[Node]
  nbrs <- empty Set
  FOR EACH (n1, n2) IN junctions DO
    IF n1 = node THEN
      ADD(n2, nbrs))
    ELSE IF n2 = node THEN
      ADD(n1, nbrs)
    END IF
  END FOR
  RETURN nbrs
END FUNCTION

FUNCTION ALL_NEIGHBOURS(node: Node, wings: Dictionary, junctions: List[Pair[Node, Node]]) -> Set[Node])
  w <- GET_WING(node)
  wingGraph <- wings[w]
  RETURN INTRA_WING_NEIGHBOURS(node, wingGraph) UNION INTER_WING_NEIGHBOURS(node, junctions)
END FUNCTION

PROCEDURE SHORTEST_PATHS_DICT_CONSTRUCTOR(graph: Graph, start: Vertex, keyNodes: List[Vertex], dist: Dictionary, paths: Dictionary, wings: Dictionary, junctions: List[Pair[Node, Node]])
   keyNodeSet <- SET(keyNodes)
   visitedKeyNodes <- empty Set
   visited <- empty Set

   pq <- empty Priority Queue
   INSERT(pq, 0, [])
   WHILE NOT IS_EMPTY(pq) DO
      (cost, path) <- POP(pq)
      current <- LAST(path)
      IF current IN visited THEN
          CONTINUE
      END IF
      ADD(current, visited)
      IF current IN keyNodesSet THEN
          paths[start][current] <- path
          dist[start][current] <- cost
          ADD(current, visitedKeyNodes)
      END IF

      IF SIZE(visitedKeyNodes) = LENGTH(keyNodes) THEN
          RETURN
      END IF

      FOREACH neighbour IN ALL_NEIGHBOURS(current, wings, junctions) DO
          IF neighbour NOT IN visited THEN
              edgeWeight <- graph.GET_EDGE_WEIGHT(current, neighbour)
              newPath <- COPY(path)
              APPEND(neighbour, newPath)
              INSERT(pq, cost + edgeWeight, newPath)
          END IF
      END FOR
   END WHILE
END PROCEDURE

FUNCTION STATE_SPACE_SEARCH(current: Vertex, remaining: List[Vertex], currentCost: Integer, order: List[Vertex], dist: Dictionary, exitA: Vertex, exitB: Vertex, bestCost, Integer, bestOrder: List[Vertex]) -> Record{cost: Integer, order: List[Vertex}}

   costToExitB <- currentCost + GET(dist[current, exitB, INFINITY)
   IF currentCost > bestCost OR (costToExitA > bestCost AND costToExitB > bestCost) THEN
      RETURN {cost: bestCost, order: bestOrder}
   END IF
 
   IF LENGTH(remaining) = 0 THEN
      costA <- GET(dist[current], exitA, INFINITY)
      costB <- GET(dist[current], exitB, INFINITY)
      IF costA < costB THEN
          chosenExit <- exitA
          exitCost <- costA
      ELSE
          chosenExit <- exitB
          exitCost <- costB
      END IF

      finalCost <- currentCost + exitCost

          newOrder <- COPY(order)
          APPEND(chosenExit, newOrder)
          RETURN {cost: finalCost, order: newOrder}
      ELSE
          RETURN {cost: bestCost, order: bestOrder}
      END IF

      stepCost <- GET(dist[current], supply, INFINITY)
